```{r}
source("scripts/define_plate_maps.R")
library(ggplot2)
x <- data.table::fread("data/counts/batch_results_TEMP_MEASURE_SIZE.csv")
x <- x[, time := substr(image_key, nchar(image_key) - 8, nchar(image_key) )]
x <- x[, base_key := substr(image_key, 1, nchar(image_key) - 10)]
x <- split(x,f=x$base_key)

meta <- do.call(rbind,lapply(paste0(names(x),"_00d00h00m"),get_meta))

meta <- data.table(meta)

# add a base_key column so meta and x line up
meta[, base_key := names(x)]

# build a grouping key
meta[, grp := paste(cellLine, experiment, plateID, ploidy, glucose, sep="|")]

# split the base_keys by grp
groups <- split(meta$base_key, meta$grp)

# for each group, rbindlist the corresponding x’s
x_merged <- lapply(groups, function(bk) 
  rbindlist(x[bk], use.names=TRUE, fill=TRUE)
)

names(x_merged) <- names(groups)
```

```{r}
smm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(x_merged), function(grp) {
  dtg <- x_merged[[grp]]

  cnt <- dtg[, {
    alive_idx <- predicted_label_name == "alive" & !is.na(cell_size_px)
    sz <- cell_size_px[alive_idx]
    qs <- if (length(sz)) stats::quantile(sz, probs=c(.10,.50,.90), na.rm=TRUE, names=FALSE) else c(NA_real_,NA_real_,NA_real_)
    .(
      alive = sum(predicted_label_name=="alive", na.rm=TRUE),
      dead  = sum(predicted_label_name=="dead",  na.rm=TRUE),
      sz_10 = qs[1],
      sz_median = qs[2],
      sz_90 = qs[3]
    )
  }, by=.(time)]

  m <- stringr::str_match(cnt$time, "(\\d{2})d(\\d{2})h")
  cnt[, hours := as.integer(m[,2])*24 + as.integer(m[,3])]

  flds <- stringr::str_split(grp, "\\|")[[1]]
  cnt[, c("cellLine","experiment","plateID","ploidy","glucose") :=
        list(flds[1],flds[2],flds[3],flds[4],flds[5])]

  cnt
}))


ploidy_map <- list(
  'SUM-159-chem' = c("2N"=2.0, "4N"=4.0),
  'SNU668'       = c("high"=5.2, "low"=2.6),
  'MCF10A'       = c("4N"=4.0, "2N"=2.0),
  'MDA-MB-231'   = c("parental"=4.4, "3N"=3.5),
  'SUM-159-fuse' = c("2N"=2.0, "4N"=4.0)
)

smm$ploidy_val    <- NA_real_
smm$ploidy_metric <- NA_real_

for (cline in intersect(names(ploidy_map), unique(smm$cellLine))) {
  map <- ploidy_map[[cline]]
  idx <- smm$cellLine == cline

  smm$ploidy_val[idx] <- unname(map[smm$ploidy[idx]])
  baseline <- min(map)
  smm$ploidy_metric[idx] <- smm$ploidy_val[idx] - baseline
  smm$baseline <- baseline
}

smm <- smm[!is.na(smm$ploidy_metric),]

saveRDS(smm,"data/counts/size_and_counts.Rds")
```

```{r}
# estimate_am_integral.R
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

stan <- readRDS("data/stan_ready_data.Rds")

trapz <- function(t, y) { o <- order(t); t <- t[o]; y <- y[o]; if (length(t) < 2) return(NA_real_); sum((t[-1]-t[-length(t)])*(y[-1]+y[-length(y)])/2, na.rm=TRUE) }

fit_cam <- function(y, x1, x2){
  ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x1) & is.finite(x2)
  y <- y[ok]; x1 <- x1[ok]; x2 <- x2[ok]
  if (length(y) < 4) return(c(c=NA_real_, a=NA_real_, m=NA_real_, rmse=NA_real_))
  
  # objective: SSE for y ≈ c + a*x1 + m*x2
  obj <- function(p) {
    r <- y - (p[1] + p[2]*x1 + p[3]*x2)
    sum(r*r)
  }
  
  # sensible start: nonnegative OLS, clipped
  b0 <- try(coef(lm(y ~ x1 + x2)), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(b0, "try-error") || any(!is.finite(b0))) b0 <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
  p0 <- pmax(0, as.numeric(b0)[1:3])
  if (all(p0 == 0)) p0 <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
  
  # bounded optimization
  opt <- optim(
    par = p0,
    fn = obj,
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(0, 0, 0),
    control = list(maxit = 10000, factr = 1e7)  # tighter than default, still reasonable
  )
  
  # if it looks like it got stuck, do a couple of cheap restarts
  if (!is.null(opt$convergence) && opt$convergence != 0) {
    best <- opt
    for (s in 1:4) {
      p_try <- pmax(0, p0 * exp(rnorm(3, 0, 1)))
      opt2 <- optim(par = p_try, fn = obj, method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(0,0,0),
                    control = list(maxit = 10000, factr = 1e7))
      if (opt2$value < best$value) best <- opt2
    }
    opt <- best
  }
  
  c_hat <- opt$par[1]; a_hat <- opt$par[2]; m_hat <- opt$par[3]
  pred <- c_hat + a_hat*x1 + m_hat*x2
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((y - pred)^2))
  
  c(c = unname(c_hat), a = unname(a_hat), m = unname(m_hat), rmse = rmse)
}

fit_cam <- function(y, x1, x2){
  ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x1)
  y <- y[ok]; x1 <- x1[ok]
  if (length(y) < 3) return(c(c=0, a=NA_real_, m=0, rmse=NA_real_))
  
  # objective: SSE for y ≈ a * x1
  obj <- function(a)
    sum((y - a * x1)^2)
  
  # sensible start from clipped OLS
  a0 <- sum(x1 * y) / sum(x1 * x1)
  if (!is.finite(a0) || a0 < 0) a0 <- 0.1
  
  opt <- optim(
    par    = a0,
    fn     = obj,
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower  = 0
  )
  
  a_hat <- opt$par
  pred  <- a_hat * x1
  rmse  <- sqrt(mean((y - pred)^2))
  
  c(c = 0, a = unname(a_hat), m = 0, rmse = rmse)
}



# well metadata
line_names <- names(stan$line_map)[match(stan$line_id, unname(stan$line_map))]
well_meta <- tibble(
  well = seq_len(stan$N_wells),
  cellLine = line_names,
  ploidy_metric = as.numeric(stan$ploidy_metric),
  ploidy_val=as.numeric(stan$ploidy_abs),
  exp_id = stan$exp_id,
  G0 = as.numeric(stan$G0_per_well)
)


# glucose back-calc consistent with Stan (as before), but keep t_last per well
gluc_long <- tibble(
  well = stan$well_idx_gluc,
  t = stan$t_grid[stan$grid_idx_gluc],
  lum = as.numeric(stan$lum_obs),
  dil = as.numeric(stan$dilution),
  cens = as.integer(stan$is_censored)
) %>%
  left_join(well_meta %>% select(well, exp_id), by="well") %>%
  mutate(
    a_cal = stan$calib_a_fixed[exp_id],
    b_cal = stan$calib_b_fixed[exp_id],
    Ghat = pmax(0, (lum - b_cal) / (a_cal * pmax(dil, 1e-12)))
  ) %>%
  group_by(well) %>%
  summarise(
    t_last = max(t, na.rm=TRUE),
    G_last = {
      g_last <- Ghat[t == t_last]
      c_last <- cens[t == t_last]
      if (any(c_last == 0, na.rm=TRUE)) median(g_last[c_last == 0], na.rm=TRUE) else median(g_last, na.rm=TRUE)
    },
    any_cens_last = any(cens[t == t_last] == 1, na.rm=TRUE),
    .groups="drop"
  )

# counts, but truncated to t_last (per well)
counts_long <- tibble(
  well = stan$well_idx_count,
  rep = stan$rep_id_count,
  t = stan$t_grid[stan$grid_idx_count],
  NL = as.numeric(stan$N_obs),
  ND = as.numeric(stan$D_obs)
) %>%
  left_join(gluc_long %>% select(well, t_last), by="well") %>%
  filter(is.finite(t_last), t <= t_last) %>%
  group_by(well, rep) %>%
  summarise(
    B0 = (NL+ND)[which.min(t)],
    Bt = (NL+ND)[which.max(t)],
    AUC_NL = trapz(t, NL),
    .groups="drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(dB = pmax(0,Bt - B0))


# assemble regression rows
well_df <- well_meta %>%
  left_join(counts_long, by="well") %>%
  left_join(gluc_long, by="well") %>%
  mutate(Gcons = pmax(0, G0 - G_last)) %>%
  filter(is.finite(Gcons), is.finite(dB), is.finite(AUC_NL))

well_df <- well_df[well_df$G0!=25,]

# fit per cellLine × ploidy_metric
fits <- well_df %>%
  group_by(cellLine, ploidy_metric,ploidy_val) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    tmp = list(fit_cam(Gcons, dB, AUC_NL)),
    c = tmp[[1]]["c"],
    a = tmp[[1]]["a"],
    m = tmp[[1]]["m"],
    rmse = tmp[[1]]["rmse"],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  select(-tmp) %>%
  arrange(cellLine, ploidy_metric)

fits <- split(fits,f=fits$cellLine)
fits <- do.call(rbind,lapply(fits,function(fi){
  fi$v_ratio <- fi$ploidy_val/min(fi$ploidy_val) 
  fi
}))
print(fits)

# write.csv(fits, "data/yield_estimates_am_by_group.csv", row.names=FALSE)

# --- Visualization of per-well fit quality ------------------------------------
plot_df <- well_df %>%
  left_join(fits, by=c("cellLine","ploidy_metric")) %>%
  mutate(
    ploidy_level = ifelse(abs(ploidy_metric) < 1e-9, "low", "high"),
    G_pred = c + a*dB + m*AUC_NL,
    resid = Gcons - G_pred
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(Gcons, G_pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0) +
  facet_grid(ploidy_level ~ cellLine, scales="free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Observed Gcons (G0 - G_last)", y="Predicted (c + a*dB + m*AUC)")+
  ggtitle("Estimating biomass yield (1/a) and maintenance (m) glucose costs")

p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(Gcons, dB)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm")+
  geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0) +
  facet_grid(ploidy_level ~ cellLine, scales="free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="glucose consumed", y="cells added")
```

```{r}
# ODE: glucose (G) gets consumed (no replenishment), alive cells (A) grow when G is available,
# and start dying when G is ~depleted. Dead cells (D) accumulate.
library(deSolve)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

ode_fun <- function(t, y, p){
  with(as.list(c(y,p)), {
    # glucose-dependent "growth" (Monod/Michaelis-Menten-like)
    fG <- G/(K + G)

    # death switches on as glucose falls (Hill on "lack of glucose")
    lack <- (G_crit^h)/(G_crit^h + G^h)   # ~0 when G>>G_crit, ~1 when G<<G_crit
    d_rate <- d0 + d1*lack

    dA <-  r*fG*A - d_rate*A
    dD <-  d_rate*A

    # consume glucose proportional to alive cells and their growth-related demand
    dG <- -cA*A - cGrow*(r*fG*A)
    if (G <= 0 && dG < 0) dG <- 0         # keep G from going negative due to numerics

    list(c(G=dG, A=dA, D=dD))
  })
}

# initial conditions
y0 <- c(G = 10,   # starting glucose (arbitrary units)
        A = 5e2,  # alive cells
        D = 0)    # dead cells

# parameters
p <- c(
  r = 0.03,      # max net growth rate (per hour)
  K = 1.0,       # half-sat glucose for growth
  d0 = 0.001,    # baseline death rate
  d1 = 0.06,     # extra death when glucose absent
  G_crit = 0.2,  # glucose level where death ramps
  h = 6,         # steepness of death switch
  cA = 2e-6,     # maintenance glucose consumption per alive cell
  cGrow = .003     # additional glucose cost per unit growth
)

times <- seq(0, 24*5, by=0.1)  # hours

out <- as.data.frame(ode(y = y0, times = times, func = ode_fun, parms = p, method="lsoda"))
out$N <- out$A + out$D

t_end <- max(out$time)

# option B (usually better): end when glucose essentially depleted
# t_end <- out$time[which(out$G <= 0.01)[1]]
# if (is.na(t_end)) t_end <- max(out$time)

row0 <- out[out$time==min(out$time),][1,]
rowE <- out[out$time==t_end,][1,]

B0   <- row0$N
Bend <- rowE$N
dB   <- Bend - B0

G0   <- row0$G
Gend <- rowE$G
dG   <- G0 - Gend   # consumed

labsB <- data.frame(
  x = c(0, t_end, t_end),
  y = c(B0, Bend, (B0+Bend)/2),
  label = c(
    sprintf("B[0]==%.1f", B0),
    sprintf("B[end]==%.1f", Bend),
    sprintf("Delta*B==%.1f", dB)
  )
)

labsG <- data.frame(
  x = c(0, t_end, t_end),
  y = c(G0, Gend, (G0+Gend)/2),
  label = c(
    sprintf("G[0]==%.2f", G0),
    sprintf("G[end]==%.2f", abs(Gend)),
    sprintf("Delta*G==%.2f", dG)
  )
)


# ---- CELLS PLOT (A/D/N) with B0/Bend lines and a bracket ----
colnames(out)[3:5] <- c("alive","dead","total")
df_cells <- melt(out[,c("time","alive","dead","total")], id.vars="time", variable.name="state", value.name="value")

p_cells <- ggplot(df_cells, aes(time, value, color=state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth=0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=B0, linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.5, color="black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=Bend, linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.5, color="black") +
  geom_segment(aes(x=t_end, xend=t_end, y=B0, yend=Bend),
             inherit.aes=FALSE,
             arrow=arrow(ends="both", type="closed", length=unit(0.18,"cm")),
             linewidth=0.8, color="black")+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.02, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill="white", color="black", linewidth=0.2),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill="white", color=NA),
        legend.key.width  = unit(0.5, "lines"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "lines"),
    legend.spacing.x  = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    legend.spacing.y  = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    legend.box.margin = margin(1,1,1,1),
    legend.text = element_text(size=8)
  )+
  geom_label(data=labsB, aes(x=x, y=y, label=label), inherit.aes=FALSE,
             hjust=c(0,1,1), vjust=c(-0.5,-0.5,0.5), size=3.2,
             label.size=0.2, fill="white", color="black",parse=T)+
  labs(x="hours", y="cell count", color=NULL)+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, .25)))

p_cells
```

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

stan_data <- readRDS("data/stan_ready_data.Rds")

plot_well_splines <- function(stan_data, well = 1) {
  stopifnot(well >= 1, well <= stan_data$N_wells)

  # --- counts for this well (NL, ND) ---
  dc <- tibble(
    well = stan_data$well_idx_count,
    t    = stan_data$t_grid[stan_data$grid_idx_count],
    NL   = as.numeric(stan_data$N_obs),
    ND   = as.numeric(stan_data$D_obs)
  ) %>%
    filter(well == !!well) %>%
    group_by(t) %>%
    summarise(
      NL = mean(NL, na.rm=TRUE),
      ND = mean(ND, na.rm=TRUE),
      .groups="drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(t)

  # total N as implied by continuity: N = NL + ND
  dc <- dc %>% mutate(N = NL + ND)

  # --- implied glucose for this well ---
  exp <- stan_data$exp_id[well]
  a <- stan_data$calib_a_fixed[exp]
  b <- stan_data$calib_b_fixed[exp]

  dg <- tibble(
    well = stan_data$well_idx_gluc,
    t    = stan_data$t_grid[stan_data$grid_idx_gluc],
    lum  = as.numeric(stan_data$lum_obs),
    dil  = as.numeric(stan_data$dilution),
    cens = as.integer(stan_data$is_censored)
  ) %>%
    filter(well == !!well) %>%
    mutate(glucose_hat = pmax(0, (lum - b) / (a * pmax(dil, 1e-12)))) %>%
    group_by(t) %>%
    summarise(
      glucose = {
        g <- glucose_hat; c <- cens
        if (any(c == 0, na.rm=TRUE)) median(g[c == 0], na.rm=TRUE) else median(g, na.rm=TRUE)
      },
      .groups="drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(t)


  

  # return both plots (counts first)
  list(counts = dc, glucose = dg)
}

# Example:
res <- plot_well_splines(stan_data, well = 20)

dc <- res$counts

dc$N <- dc$ND + dc$NL

dc <- reshape2::melt(dc,id.vars="t")


p <- ggplot(dc,aes(x=t,y=value,color=variable))+
  geom_point()
p
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# REFACTORED ANALYSIS BLOCK
# Requires: 'smm' (size/count data) and 'fits' (regression results)
# ==============================================================================

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# --- 1. Prepare Reference Size Data from 'smm' --------------------------------
# We work on a copy of smm to extract 24h sizes
dt_size <- as.data.table(smm)

# Calculate median size at 24h (20h-28h window) per cellLine/ploidy_metric
size_stats <- dt_size[hours >= 20 & hours <= 28, .(
  area_24h = median(sz_median, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(cellLine, ploidy_metric)]

# Calculate geometry-based volume proxies
size_stats[, vol_flat   := area_24h^1.0]
size_stats[, vol_sphere := area_24h^1.5]

# --- 2. Merge Size Data into Fits ---------------------------------------------
# Create the analysis table by merging regression fits with size data
fits_analyzed <- as.data.table(fits) %>%
  left_join(size_stats, by = c("cellLine", "ploidy_metric")) %>%
  as.data.table()

# Check for missing size data (safety check)
if (any(is.na(fits_analyzed$vol_flat))) {
  warning("Some conditions are missing 24h size data. Ratios may be NA.")
}

# --- 3. Compute Baselines and Ratios ------------------------------------------

# A. Identify Baseline Rows
# We define the 'baseline' as the condition with the lowest ploidy_metric for each cellLine
baseline_vals <- fits_analyzed[order(ploidy_metric), .SD[1], by = cellLine]

# Select only the columns we need for the baseline reference
baseline_ref <- baseline_vals[, .(
  cellLine, 
  a_base = a, 
  vol_flat_base = vol_flat, 
  vol_sphere_base = vol_sphere
)]

# B. Merge Baseline values back into the main table
fits_analyzed <- merge(fits_analyzed, baseline_ref, by = "cellLine")

# C. Calculate Ratios and Normalized Costs
fits_analyzed[, `:=`(
  # Cost Ratio: (Cost High) / (Cost Low)
  ratio_cost = a / a_base,
  
  # Volume Ratios: (Vol High) / (Vol Low)
  ratio_vol_flat   = vol_flat / vol_flat_base,
  ratio_vol_sphere = vol_sphere / vol_sphere_base,
  
  # Absolute Biomass Cost: Glucose spent per unit volume
  cost_bio_flat   = a / vol_flat,
  cost_bio_sphere = a / vol_sphere
)]

print(head(fits_analyzed))

# --- 4. Plotting --------------------------------------------------------------

p_cell <- ggplot(fits_analyzed, aes(x = factor(ploidy_metric), y = a, fill = cellLine)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~cellLine, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Per-Cell Construction Cost (Unadjusted)", 
       subtitle = "Metric: Glucose consumed to build one cell",
       y = "Cost (Glucose / Cell)", 
       x = "Ploidy Shift")

print(p_cell)

# Plot A: Absolute Biomass Cost (Efficiency Check)
# Interpretation: Lower bars = More efficient (Cheaper to build biomass)
p1 <- ggplot(fits_analyzed, aes(x = factor(ploidy_metric), y = cost_bio_flat, fill = cellLine)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~cellLine, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Biomass Construction Cost (Assumption: Flat/Pancake)", 
       subtitle = "Metric: Glucose consumed per unit Volume (Flat Proxy)",
       y = "Cost (Glucose / Vol_Flat)", 
       x = "Ploidy Shift")

p2 <- ggplot(fits_analyzed, aes(x = factor(ploidy_metric), y = cost_bio_sphere, fill = cellLine)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~cellLine, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Biomass Construction Cost (Assumption: Spherical)", 
       subtitle = "Metric: Glucose consumed per unit Volume (Sphere Proxy)",
       y = "Cost (Glucose / Vol_Sphere)", 
       x = "Ploidy Shift")

print(p1)
print(p2)

# Plot B: Metabolic Scaling (The Beta Exponent)
# We plot log(Cost Ratio) vs log(Volume Ratio)
# Reshape for plotting both assumptions on one graph
scaling_data <- rbind(
  fits_analyzed[, .(cellLine, ploidy_metric, vol_ratio = ratio_vol_flat,   cost_ratio = ratio_cost, Assumption="Flat")],
  fits_analyzed[, .(cellLine, ploidy_metric, vol_ratio = ratio_vol_sphere, cost_ratio = ratio_cost, Assumption="Sphere")]
)

p3 <- ggplot(scaling_data, aes(x = vol_ratio, y = cost_ratio, color = Assumption)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # Reference: Isometric Scaling (beta = 1) -> Cost scales linearly with Volume
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + 
  annotate("text", x = 1.1, y = 1.2, label = "Isometric (beta=1)", angle = 45, hjust=0) +
  
  # Regression lines (forced through origin 0,0)
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ 0 + x, se = FALSE, aes(group = Assumption), linewidth=0.5) +
  
  # Log-Log scales allow us to see the power law behavior
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4)) +
  
  facet_wrap(~cellLine) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Metabolic Scaling: Cost vs Volume",
    subtitle = "Slope (beta) < 1 implies economy of scale (efficiency)",
    x = "Volume Ratio (High / Low)",
    y = "Glucose Cost Ratio (High / Low)"
  )

print(p3)

# --- 5. Estimate Scaling Exponent (Beta) --------------------------------------
# Model: Cost_Ratio ~ Volume_Ratio ^ beta
# Log-Log: log(Cost_Ratio) ~ beta * log(Vol_Ratio)

calc_beta <- function(dt, vol_col) {
  # We force regression through the origin (0,0) because Ratio 1:1 is fixed by definition
  tryCatch({
    # Check if we have enough points (need at least one non-baseline point for a meaningful slope)
    if (nrow(dt) < 2) return(NA_real_)
    model <- lm(log(ratio_cost) ~ 0 + log(get(vol_col)), data = dt)
    return(coef(model)[1])
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

betas <- fits_analyzed[, .(
  beta_flat   = calc_beta(.SD, "ratio_vol_flat"),
  beta_sphere = calc_beta(.SD, "ratio_vol_sphere")
), by = cellLine]

print("--- Estimated Cost Scaling Exponents (beta) ---")
print("beta = 1.0 : Linear scaling (2x Volume costs 2x Glucose)")
print("beta < 1.0 : Economy of Scale (Larger cells are cheaper per unit vol)")
print("beta > 1.0 : Diseconomy (Larger cells are more expensive)")
print(betas)
```
